observations: Canon DSLR camera body with an attached lens and lens cap.
Model badge on the front identifies it as an 'EOS 650D' in photo 0.
Lens barrel shows focal length markings 18, 24, 35, and 55 in photos 0 and 2.
The articulating rear screen is flipped closed (facing the body) in photo 1.
The top view in photo 2 shows the mode dial, shutter button, and 'Canon' branding on the lens.
The camera appears to be in good cosmetic condition with no obvious external damage.

claims.evidence: Photos 0, 1, and 2 show the exterior is free of significant scuffs or dirt.
Photo 0 shows the 'EOS 650D' badge, which is the same model.
Photo 0 and 2 show the 18-55mm focal length markings on the lens barrel.
No photos show the camera powered on, the screen active, or any images captured by the device.

risks.risk: The articulating screen may be cracked, have dead pixels, or a faulty ribbon cable.
risks.proof: A photo of the screen flipped out and powered on showing the menu or live view.

risks.risk: The image sensor may have fungus, dust, or scratches.
risks.proof: A clear photo of the sensor with the lens removed.
risks.if_unproven: as requiring professional cleaning or sensor replacement

risks.risk: The lens may have internal mold (fungus) or a failed autofocus motor.
risks.proof: A video showing the lens focusing and a photo of the glass elements against a light source.
risks.if_unproven: as a manual-focus-only lens with optical defects

risks.risk: The shutter may be near its end of life or non-functional.
risks.proof: A screenshot of the shutter count or a photo of the camera in Live View mode.

risks.risk: Essential accessories like the battery and charger may be missing.
risks.proof: A photo showing the battery and charger included.

proof_requests: Photo of the screen flipped out and powered on.
Photo of the sensor with the lens removed.
Photo of the lens glass looking for fungus.
Confirmation of whether a battery and charger are included.
response.reason: The camera and lens are clearly identified by the photos. Because there is no proof of functionality (screen is closed, no power-on shots), it is priced at the lowest end of the DSLR market as a worst-case scenario for parts or repair.
